question.worked_solution:
Let $u=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(-{sin}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

 Since ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{-1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$
